items.title: Constructing Symmetrical Eyes
items.explanation: To draw symmetrical eyes, start by drawing a supporting line XY. Use an unmarked ruler and compass to find the perpendicular bisector of XY: take equal radii from points X and Y above XY to mark point A, then below XY to mark point B. The line AB is the perpendicular bisector. Join A and B; their intersection with XY will be the midpoint, forming a 90-degree angle.

items.title: Constructing Perpendicular Bisector
items.explanation: To construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment XY: 1) Draw arcs above XY with equal radii from X and Y to find point A. 2) Draw arcs below XY with equal radii from X and Y to find point B. 3) Join AB; this line is the required perpendicular bisector.
